question: what classes do I need to take for the psychology major
answer:
The Psychology BA (Bachelor of Arts) requires [1]:
- Required courses: PSYC 101 INTRODUCTION TO PSYCHOLOGY; PSYC 242 STATISTICS; PSYC 303 RESEARCH METHODS IN PSYCHOLOGY and PSYC 304 DATA ANALYSIS IN PSYCHOLOGY.
- Select 1 course from each category:
  1. Social and Organizational: PSYC 226 SOCIAL PSYCHOLOGY; PSYC 345 WORKPLACE PSYCHOLOGY.
  2. Cognition and Perception: PSYC 202 PSYCHOLOGY OF LEARNING; PSYC 209 PSYCHOLOGY OF PERCEPTION; PSYC 227 COGNITIVE PSYCHOLOGY.
  3. Developmental: PSYC 212 PSYCHOLOGY OF AGING; PSYC 241 DEVELOPMENTAL PSYCHOLOGY; PSYC 263 CHILD PSYCHOLOGY; PSYC 347 ADOLESCENT PSYCHOLOGY.
  4. Socio-cultural Perspectives: PSYC 231 MULTICULTURAL PSYCHOLOGY; PSYC 239 CROSS-CULTURAL PSYCHOLOGY; PSYC 307 PSYCHOLOGY OF YOGA; PSYC 311 PSYCHOLOGY OF GENDER; PSYC 335 SEXUALITIES AND GENDER IDENTITIES: LGBTQA+; PSYC 349 PSYCHOLOGY OF WOMEN.
  5. Clinical Perspectives: PSYC 314 PSYCHOPATHOLOGY; PSYC 321 THEORIES OF PERSONALITY; PSYC 357 CHILDHOOD DISORDERS.
  6. Brain and Behavior: PSYC 310 NEUROPSYCHOLOGY; PSYC 352 BEHAVIORAL NEUROSCIENCE; PSYC 353 COGNITIVE NEUROSCIENCE; PSYC 355 NEUROPSYCHOPHARMACOLOGY.
  7. Fieldwork/Independent Research: PSYC 319 ADULT PSYCHOLOGY FIELDWORK; PSYC 320 PSYCHOPATHOLOGY FIELDWORK; PSYC 339 FIELDWORK WITH ADOLESCENTS; PSYC 358 CHILDHOOD DISORDERS FIELDWORK; PSYC 367 FIELDWORK WITH CHILDREN; PSYC 368 FIELDWORK IN FORENSIC PSYCHOLOGY; PSYC 472 ADVANCED RESEARCH.
  8. Capstone Seminar: PSYC 430 CAPSTONE SEMINAR TOPICS IN PSYCHOLOGY; PSYC 431 CAPSTONE SEMINAR: CHILD MALTREATMENT; PSYC 432 CAPSTONE SEMINAR: PSYCHOLOGY OF CULTS; PSYC 433 CAPSTONE SEMINAR: PSYCHOPATHY; PSYC 434 CAPSTONE SEMINAR: CULTURAL NATURE OF DEVELOPMENT; PSYC 436 CAPSTONE SEMINAR: PSYCHOANALYTIC THOUGHT - UNDERSTANDING THE UNCONSCIOUS; PSYC 437 CAPSTONE SEMINAR: PSYCHOLOGY OF HAPPINESS; PSYC 438 CAPSTONE SEMINAR: SOCIAL JUSTICE AND PSYCHOLOGY; PSYC 439 CAPSTONE SEMINAR: PHENOMENOLOGIAL PSYCHOLOGY; PSYC 440 CAPSTONE SEMINAR: EYEWITNESS MEMORY; PSYC 450 CAPSTONE SEMINAR IN COGNITIVE DEVELOPMENT; PSYC 451 CAPSTONE SEMINAR: BLACK PSYCHOLOGY.
- Additional Psychology Course: Select 1 Course (no course options are listed).
- Career Pathways required courses: PATH 001 CAREER PATHWAYS MOD 1; PATH 001 CAREER PATHWAYS MOD 1; PATH 003 CAREER PATHWAYS MOD 3. [1]
Psychology Minor is also published. [1]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SO-BA-PSYC)

question: how many credits is a minor and can i double count courses with my major?
answer:
A minor must include between 16 and 24 credits, including non-General Education prerequisites and excluding lab science course credits. Courses required for your primary or secondary major may count toward your minor, but no more than half of the minor credits may overlap. [1]

question: what is cmps 147 about and what are the prereqs

question: What general education requirements do I have to finish before I graduate, and how many credits is the whole gen ed thing?
answer:
Ramapo’s general education curriculum is ten courses: First Year Seminar, Social Science Inquiry, Critical Reading & Writing 102, and Studies in the Arts & Humanities; one course each in Global Awareness, Historical Perspectives, Scientific Reasoning, and Quantitative Reasoning; and one course in two of three distribution categories. [1][3] Critical Reading & Writing 102 and Quantitative Reasoning must be completed within the first 64 credits. [1] Section 1 says at least one distribution course must be offered by a school other than the one housing your major. Section 5 says that, starting Fall 2026, the “out of school requirement” is no longer enforced in degree audit tools; the pages differ on this condition. [1][5] Section 5 lists the distribution categories as Culture and Creativity, Values and Ethics, and Social Systems and Society. [5]
The catalog says the curriculum “should not exceed 41 credits”; it does not give an exact total. [4]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/curriculum-and-assessment/) [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#general-education) [4](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#integrity-of-degree-programs1) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/home/comprehensive-academic-plan/resources/)

question: what should a freshman in business take first semester
answer:

For the seminar, you could consider the Business & Politics offerings: INTD 101-08 Investment Literacy and the Power of Compound Interest; INTD 101-17 Economics, Business, and You; INTD 101-32 Diplomacy and Discord: Cooperation and Conflict in Contemporary Global Society; INTD 101-33 An Introduction to Investing and the Stock Market; INTD 101-35 World Affairs in the Digital Age; or INTD 101-42 Historical and Practical Considerations of Economics and Finance [5]. question: whats the difference between a major, a minor and a certificate at ramapo?
answer:
A major is required for every undergraduate degree. Its requirements are at least 40 and no more than 64 credits, including major-specific concentrations, tracks, and prerequisites; they typically make up about half of the degree program. [9]

A minor is supplemental and distinct from the major, adding depth and breadth to an undergraduate degree. It must include 16–24 credits; no more than half of its required credits may also count toward a primary or secondary major. [8]

An academic certificate is a coherent program of study, usually made up of credit-bearing courses; it may also include non-credit learning experiences. Certificates can be undergraduate, graduate, or doctoral. Graduate certificates require at least 9 credits beyond the bachelor’s level, and doctoral certificates require at least 12 beyond the master’s level. Certificates are not graduation requirements and are removed from the degree audit. [7]

Sources: [7](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#certificate-programs1) [8](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#integrity-of-degree-programs1) [9](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#integrity-of-degree-programs1)

question: do you have a major for communication arts and what does it require
answer:
Yes. Ramapo offers Communication Arts, a Bachelor of Arts (BA), with Digital Journalism and Writing or Global Communication and Media concentrations. [1]

Both concentrations require COMM 204 and 221, a 300-level history/theory/criticism course (select 1), CNTP 388 co-op/internship, and PATH 001, 002 and 003. [1]

Digital Journalism and Writing also requires COMM 231 and one of COMM 203, 227 or 234; COMM 208, 303, 324, and one of 226, 311 or 319; two digital storytelling courses; one digital tools course; one specialized writing course; and one capstone portfolio course. [1]

Global Communication and Media also requires COMM 203, 232 and 267; COMM 234, 266 and 318; one media production course; two media criticism/analysis courses; two media writing courses; one capstone portfolio course; and one elective. [1]

For the exact course choices in each category, see the [Communication Arts catalog](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/AH-BA-COMM). [1]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/AH-BA-COMM)

question: which majors are the easiest? I want something that gets me a good job
answer:
Ramapo’s pages don’t identify the easiest majors or say that any major will get you a good job. The major-advising page says, “majors don’t get you a job. Job experience does.” [1]

To explore a fit:
1. Read the catalog, attend School events, ask questions, and talk with advisors and students. [1]
2. Use FOCUS 2 to explore careers and majors: https://www.focus2career.com/Portal/Login.cfm?SID=569; access code: ramapo430. [4]
3. Explore career options and labor-market trends on O*NET: http://www.onetonline.org/. [6]
4. Connect with faculty and visit the Career Center to speak with your Career Advisor. [2]
5. Consider classes that help you decide, talk with faculty in those majors, and get co-op or internship experience before graduating. [1]
6. For co-op, call or visit the Career Center at C 209 to schedule an appointment with your career advisor; they’ll check eligibility and begin the application process. [5] Handshake can help you search for jobs and co-op internships; register and post a resume. [5]

Center for Student Success (Academic Advising): success@ramapo.edu; (201) 684-7441. [1] Cahill Career Development Center: careercenter@ramapo.edu; Main Office (201) 684-7444; ASB Office (201) 684-7675. [2]
